sovereign_country.strategic_role: 连接拉美市场的欧洲商贸桥梁、本地化仓配与数字游民签证

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of High-Power DC Ultra-Fast Electric Vehicle Chargers

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (continental European unitary jurisdiction; regional private-law specialties do not alter corporate and AML/CFT rules)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July, approving the consolidated text of the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), particularly Articles 4, 20–23, 33, 58–62, 78–79, 160, 209 and 210; Law 14/2013 of 27 September, Articles 15–16, for eligible formation through CIRCE.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for the registered office; the Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central) issues the company-name certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución), filed for registration in the competent Provincial Commercial Registry; a Single Electronic Document (Documento Único Electrónico, DUE) may be used through CIRCE where eligible.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital is EUR 1. Contributions must be fully paid when shares are subscribed. While capital remains below EUR 3,000, at least 20% of annual profits must be allocated to legal reserve until share capital and reserve together reach EUR 3,000; in liquidation, shareholders may be jointly liable for the shortfall to EUR 3,000. No statutory escrow account is required. Notarial and registry charges are tariff-based and are not represented by the USD 0 field above.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accepts the subscriptions and contributions set out in the incorporation deed and confirms that all subscribed shares are fully paid. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at [full Spanish address], subject to any required notification or filing. RESOLVED, that [name and identification details] be appointed [sole director/joint directors/joint and several directors], with the powers stated in the articles and appointment instrument, and that each appointee’s acceptance and statutory declarations be recorded. RESOLVED, that the directors are authorized to complete tax, registry, social security, banking, and administrative registrations and to obtain any permits required for the Company’s premises and activities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), Company Name Certification service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a negative company-name certificate listing proposed names in order of preference. Use the original certificate or the permitted electronic certificate for the notarial deed. Ensure the certificate remains valid on the deed execution date.
required_dossiers: Applicant identification and contact details
Proposed company names in order of preference
Name reservation or negative certification application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is rejected or unavailable, submit alternative names. Correct any applicant or reservation-data mismatch before signing the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Set share capital, articles, address, and governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public; CIRCE/PAE (Entrepreneur Service Point) if the electronic route is used
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles, determine the registered office, business purpose, capital and share allocation, and choose a permitted administration structure. Identify foreign shareholders and directors and obtain Spanish foreigner identification numbers (NIEs) where required. Make capital contributions directly as documented in the deed; no statutory escrow is required. A bank certificate may evidence a cash contribution, while the statutory alternative declaration may be available subject to the incorporators’ liability.
required_dossiers: Central Commercial Registry name certificate
Articles of association
Shareholder and director identification documents and NIEs, where applicable
Evidence of address and shareholder ownership details
Evidence or declaration concerning capital contributions
Powers of attorney, duly apostilled or legalized and translated where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve missing NIE, legalization, translation, capital-evidence, or article-form defects with the notary before execution. Revise any corporate-purpose wording that is unclear or impermissibly broad.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the incorporation deed and obtain tax identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public; Spanish State Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All required incorporators or properly authorized representatives execute the public deed. Request provisional NIF and file the census registration using Form 036 or the applicable CIRCE process. The incorporation transaction is generally exempt from transfer tax and stamp duty (ITP-AJD), but the required tax filing or exemption declaration must be completed as applicable.
required_dossiers: Draft and final articles of association
Name certificate
Shareholder and director identification and NIEs
Capital contribution evidence or permitted declaration
Registered-office details
Executed powers of attorney, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct deed or census-form discrepancies through the notary or AEAT. Obtain a corrected or definitive NIF after registration and update the AEAT census record.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the company and activate post-incorporation records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry for the province of the registered office; AEAT; applicable Social Security Treasury (Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarial deed and required supporting documents to the Provincial Commercial Registry, directly or through the notary/CIRCE. Complete applicable census, tax, beneficial-ownership, accounting-book legalization, and employer/social-security registrations before commencing relevant operations. Obtain the registered deed and definitive NIF.
required_dossiers: Notarial incorporation deed
Articles of association
Provisional NIF and census filing evidence
ITP-AJD exemption filing evidence, where applicable
Identification and representation documents
Beneficial-ownership information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Address a registry defect notice by filing a corrected deed, supplemental notarial instrument, or missing evidence within the stated cure period. Refile after correction and verify the definitive NIF and registration particulars.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: The competent industrial authority of the autonomous community where the manufacturing premises are located; there is no single national industrial licensing board. The relevant municipality separately administers premises, construction, and activity procedures.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No generally applicable sector-specific manufacturing licence is identified for manufacture of EV charging equipment. Depending on the premises, the operator must obtain the applicable municipal activity/environmental authorization and file or register the industrial establishment and relevant installations with the autonomous-community industrial authority under applicable regional procedures and Royal Decree 559/2010.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: The environmental authority of the autonomous community in which the project is located; the Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge (Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico) is competent only where national competence applies.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Site- and process-dependent. A standalone manufacturing facility is not automatically subject to a full EIA; screening under Law 21/2013 and the applicable autonomous-community rules determines whether it is exempt, subject to simplified EIA, or subject to ordinary EIA. Environmental authorization requirements may separately apply to listed industrial activities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with the applicable integrated environmental authorization or regional/municipal permit, discharge authorization and sewer by-laws, and national and EU industrial-emissions and waste rules. No universal numerical wastewater or VOC threshold can be assigned without the process, capacity, location, and receiving system. Segregate, classify, store, and transfer hazardous and non-hazardous waste through authorized channels; obtain any required waste-producer registration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before occupation or operation, obtain applicable municipal building, first-occupation/use, and activity clearances; comply with the applicable fire-safety requirements, including the Industrial Establishments Fire Safety Regulation (Royal Decree 2267/2004) where applicable, and the Building Technical Code. Electrical installations and other regulated industrial installations must be designed, certified, inspected, and registered as required by applicable regulations and regional procedures. Meet occupational risk prevention duties under Law 31/1995, including risk assessment, prevention planning, worker information and training, and required coordination of business activities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) - Official portal: https://www.agenciatributaria.gob.es/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must obtain a Spanish NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) from the AEAT by submitting a formal application online or in person, accompanied by passport or foreign identification copy, company incorporation documents, and power of attorney if represented by an intermediary. VAT registration follows upon NIF issuance if projected or actual taxable turnover exceeds the 50,000 EUR threshold, processed via the AEAT portal with self-assessment and periodic filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available under Spanish law; tax classification is strictly determined by residency status and legal form. Non-resident entities are subject to territorial taxation on Spanish-source income only. No hybrid mismatch elections apply to entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: 50,000 EUR annual turnover threshold triggering mandatory VAT registration
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing under the Facturae standard with real-time reporting via the SII (Sistema de Información Inmediata) platform, including API submissions, digital stamping, and automated clearance procedures enforced directly by the AEAT.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate applies to goods exported outside the EU upon issuance of a zero-rated invoice and proof that goods have left Spanish territory. Offshore services are zero-rated per place-of-supply rules if supplied to non-EU customers with no permanent establishment in Spain. All claims require substantiation that the transaction qualifies as an export or offshore supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent zero-rating claims result in retrospective assessment of full VAT at the standard rate plus statutory interest, fines equivalent to 100% of evaded tax, and potential criminal prosecution for tax evasion under Spanish law.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain maintains a regime of unrestricted capital account convertibility with no prior approval required for profit remittances to non-resident shareholders. Current account transactions face no restrictions, while capital account movements exceeding EUR 50,000 must be notified to the Banco de España in advance. Profit remittances are permitted freely upon submission of corporate board resolutions, audited financial statements, and tax residency documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spanish exporters are not subject to mandatory surrender of export proceeds to the central bank. Exporters must submit a customs declaration and export declaration within 15 days of shipment. Proceeds may be converted into euros or foreign currency without surrender ratios, subject only to anti-money laundering reporting obligations and accurate description of goods under the relevant HS code.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for Spanish-regulated electronic money institutions licensed by the Banco de España under MiCA framework, including services from N26 Business and Revolut Business. Offshore digital EMIs face legal constraints when providing cross-border payment services to Spanish residents without local authorization or establishment.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of directors or authorized signatories is mandatory for corporate account opening and KYC interviews at Spanish commercial banks. Remote video identification is permitted only through approved fintech partners or under specific regulatory sandboxes for smaller transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership exceeding 25 percent held by non-residents without supporting documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Mercantile Registry extract confirming ownership structure, board resolution authorizing the account, and tax residency certificates for all ultimate beneficial owners

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent source of funds or capital injection declarations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements, supplier invoices, corporate resolutions, and valuation reports demonstrating legitimate business purpose and arm's length transaction

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must be executed via SEPA wire transfers to the Spanish operational account using the receiving bank's BIC code and IBAN. Purpose code 'CAP' or 'EQU' is required, supported by board resolution, capital contribution agreement, and valuation report for bank verification and regulatory reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for EV charger exports utilize SWIFT MT103 for international wire transfers or issuance of commercial letters of credit through correspondent banking networks. Accurate HS code classification (8536.90) and detailed goods description are essential for smooth customs clearance and settlement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward contracts for currency risk mitigation
Currency swaps to manage long-term liquidity and FX exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year-end; for calendar year-end, due by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deposit closes the company's registry sheet, prohibits registration of subsequent corporate resolutions, triggers coercive fines up to 0.5% of the company's capital, and may lead to dissolution and strike-off for persistent non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within seven months after tax year-end; for calendar year-end, due by 25 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties of 5% of unpaid tax plus late-payment interest, further surcharges, and administrative enforcement proceedings for continued non-payment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaración de Titularidad Real (UBO annual confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil provincial in connection with the annual accounts filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the Cuentas Anuales, within six months after fiscal year-end; calendar year-end deadline is 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to present the UBO declaration blocks the registration of the annual accounts, causes registry closure, and may trigger fines under anti-money-laundering legislation

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies if the SL meets at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive fiscal years: total assets exceed EUR 2.85 million, net annual revenue exceeds EUR 5.7 million, or average workforce exceeds 50 employees; all credit institutions, insurance entities, and listed companies are subject to audit regardless of thresholds
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad, PGC), aligned with EU-adopted IFRS; non-listed entities may apply PGC, and listed or consolidated groups apply IFRS as endorsed by the EU

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SL must keep an internal corporate register of beneficial owners and update it promptly after any ownership transfer; an annual UBO confirmation statement must be deposited together with the annual accounts and must identify all shareholders holding directly or indirectly more than 25% of capital or voting rights

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general Spanish corporate income tax rate. For tax periods beginning in 2025, qualifying micro-enterprises with prior-year net turnover below EUR 1 million generally apply 17% to the first EUR 50,000 of taxable income and 20% to the excess; qualifying small entities with prior-year net turnover below EUR 10 million generally apply 24%. Newly created entities carrying on an economic activity may generally apply 15% in the first tax period with a positive taxable base and the following period, subject to statutory exclusions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Potential relief includes the reduced rates described above, an R&D and technological innovation tax credit, and qualifying investment incentives under the Corporate Income Tax Law. Spain has no general tax holiday for ordinary charger manufacturing. Eligibility, limits, carryforwards, and regional or state-aid restrictions must be verified for each incentive.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite. Tax losses generally may be carried forward without a fixed time limit, subject to taxable-base limitation rules, minimum taxation rules, anti-abuse restrictions, and specific ownership-change limitations. The schema's suggested five-year period is not Spain's general rule.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Corporate Income Tax return, filed electronically through the Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT) electronic headquarters using an accepted electronic certificate or other authorized identification method.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; most companies also make three advance payments using Modelo 202.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Modelo 200 is due within 25 calendar days following the six months after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the usual filing window is 1–25 July of the following year, subject to official calendar and non-working-day rules. Modelo 202 advance payments are generally due 1–20 April, October, and December; qualifying entities may be exempt from making advance payments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the Spanish tax identification number (NIF), legal name, registered details, tax period, accounting period, and applicable return indicators.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign shareholder does not change the SL's Spanish resident corporate-tax status. The SL uses its Spanish NIF and reports its own Spanish tax period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify the entity as a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada and select the applicable tax regime, including any eligible reduced-rate status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not classify the Spanish SL as a non-resident merely because its shareholders are non-resident. Report qualifying newly created or turnover-based rates only where statutory conditions are met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the profit or loss from the statutory accounts before corporate-tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include the Spanish entity's worldwide accounting result, subject to applicable tax adjustments and any specific international rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile accounting profit to taxable profit, including non-deductible expenses, exempt income, depreciation differences, provisions, and other statutory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the participation exemption or other cross-border provisions only when their statutory ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, and anti-abuse requirements are satisfied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose related-party transactions where required by the return and maintain arm's-length support and prescribed documentation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include transactions with non-resident associated enterprises and ensure consistent contractual, accounting, withholding-tax, and transfer-pricing treatment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim eligible prior-period tax-loss carryforwards and tax credits, applying the relevant limits and supporting records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain evidence of the loss origin, tax-return history, ownership changes, and any applicable limitation; do not assume losses transfer to a shareholder or another group company.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the taxable base after permitted adjustments and deductions, then apply the rate applicable to the entity and tax period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder does not itself qualify the SL for a reduced rate or alter the Spanish corporate-tax rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Payments on account and withholding credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit applicable advance payments, tax withheld, and other permitted payments against the final liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile Spanish withholding certificates and Modelo 202 payments; separately assess any foreign tax credit claim and its statutory limitations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the balance payable or refundable and provide the required Spanish bank or payment details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use a payment method accepted by AEAT and ensure that any payer or bank account arrangement satisfies Spanish filing and payment requirements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: A late return filed without a prior tax-authority request generally attracts a surcharge of 1% plus 1% for each full month of delay; after 12 months, the surcharge is generally 15%, plus late-payment interest from the statutory point. A return filed after a tax-authority request may incur a tax penalty, generally 50%–150% of the unpaid amount depending on classification and aggravating factors, in addition to interest. Incorrect returns, omitted income, and failure to make required payments can trigger separate penalties. Modelo 202 non-payment may generate surcharges, interest, and penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202, advance payment on account of Corporate Income Tax, filed and paid electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Three payments per tax period, generally in April, October, and December.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally 1–20 April, 1–20 October, and 1–20 December. The applicable payment calculation method and any exemption depend on statutory conditions, including entity size and tax-period circumstances.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the NIF, legal name, tax period, and installment number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Spanish SL files under its own NIF irrespective of the residence of its shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Select the legally applicable calculation method and report the relevant prior-period liability or current-period taxable base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the statutory method consistently and retain the computation supporting the selected method.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the installment, enter any permitted credits or adjustments, and pay or report a zero amount as applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile installments to the annual Modelo 200 return and retain payment confirmations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or deficient payment may result in statutory surcharges, late-payment interest, and, where applicable, penalties under the General Tax Law. A filing or payment failure following a tax-authority request may be treated more severely than voluntary correction.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The general Spanish withholding rate on dividends paid to non-residents is 19%, subject to domestic exemptions and applicable tax treaties. EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief may eliminate withholding where its ownership, holding-period, beneficial-ownership, subject-to-tax, and anti-abuse requirements are met. A non-resident company may also qualify for a domestic exemption in specified circumstances.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, the recipient should provide the Spanish payer with a valid tax-residence certificate issued by the competent authority of the treaty country and any required beneficial-ownership and entitlement declarations. The payer applies treaty relief only where statutory procedural conditions are met and retains evidence. If the full domestic rate is withheld, the recipient may generally seek a refund from AEAT using the applicable non-resident tax refund procedure, supplying the residence certificate, payment and withholding evidence, and beneficial-ownership support. Confirm certificate validity and any Spanish filing or notification requirements for the specific payment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The general domestic non-resident withholding rate is 19% for interest and royalties, subject to statutory exemptions, including qualifying EU-related exemptions, and treaty relief. Treaty rates vary by recipient country, income characterization, beneficial ownership, and treaty conditions; no single treaty rate applies across countries. Arm's-length pricing and transfer-pricing rules remain relevant to related-party payments.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Spain generally requires related-party transaction documentation, subject to statutory exemptions. Documentation is generally not required for transactions with the same related person where the aggregate consideration does not exceed EUR 250,000 at arm's length during the tax period, subject to exceptions, including certain transactions and tax regimes. Specific documentation requirements apply to certain transactions exceeding EUR 100,000 in aggregate with the same related person and to other prescribed cases. Master File requirements generally apply to groups meeting the statutory consolidated net turnover threshold of EUR 45 million. The specific transaction, group, and exemption rules must be tested for the relevant year.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not operate a UAE-style standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime. Spanish tax authorities may nevertheless challenge arrangements lacking genuine business purpose or substance under domestic rules on simulation, conflict in the application of tax law, beneficial ownership, permanent establishment, controlled foreign companies, and treaty anti-abuse provisions. Maintain evidence of actual personnel, decision-making, assets, functions, risks, premises, and commercial rationale.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional concealment of taxable income, fabricated expenses, false invoices, or other fraudulent conduct causing unpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties depend on the conduct, tax amount, and aggravating factors and can generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, in addition to tax and interest. Tax fraud exceeding EUR 120,000 per tax and period may constitute a criminal offence under the Criminal Code, generally punishable by one to five years' imprisonment and a fine of one to six times the defrauded amount. Aggravated cases, including amounts exceeding EUR 600,000 or specified organized conduct, may carry two to six years' imprisonment and a fine of two to six times the amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face criminal liability where they personally participate, authorize, or knowingly facilitate the offence. They may also face civil or tax-administration liability under applicable statutory conditions. Imprisonment is not automatic; travel restrictions are not a standard automatic sanction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recording fictitious transactions, manipulating accounts, or knowingly claiming unsupported expenses, depreciation, tax credits, or losses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, repayment, interest, and applicable administrative penalties; criminal sanctions may apply if the conduct satisfies the elements and thresholds of a Criminal Code offence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director's liability depends on personal participation, culpability, statutory grounds, and due process. Separate accounting, commercial, or insolvency-law consequences may arise.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing related-party goods, services, financing, or intangibles outside the arm's-length range; failing to maintain required documentation; or using unsupported allocations or royalty charges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Taxable-base adjustments, tax and interest, and specific documentation or valuation penalties under the Spanish Corporate Income Tax Law and General Tax Law. Penalty amounts depend on the type of breach, the information omitted or misstated, and the tax adjustment; no single flat penalty applies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal sanctions are not automatic. Directors may be liable where statutory conditions for participation, culpable breach, or subsidiary tax liability are met.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming reduced withholding without valid residence evidence, beneficial ownership, treaty entitlement, or satisfaction of anti-abuse requirements; mischaracterizing dividends, interest, or royalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of underwithheld tax, late-payment interest, and applicable penalties. The Spanish payer may be liable for failure to withhold or remit tax; treaty relief may be denied where entitlement conditions are not met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face liability only where the relevant statutory requirements are satisfied, including culpable conduct or grounds for subsidiary liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using an entity or transaction without genuine commercial substance to conceal the true taxpayer, obtain an improper tax advantage, or disguise the beneficial owner or place of effective activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may recharacterize or disregard the arrangement under applicable anti-abuse, simulation, or conflict rules and assess tax, interest, and penalties. Criminal consequences require proof of the relevant offence and thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability depends on participation, knowledge, statutory tax-liability provisions, and the facts. Limited liability is not automatically disregarded solely because an entity is tax-inefficient.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to comply with anti-money-laundering obligations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Where the SL is a regulated obliged entity or undertakes an activity subject to the Spanish AML regime, failure to identify customers or beneficial owners, monitor transactions, retain records, or report suspicious activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Sanctions under Law 10/2010 depend on the seriousness and classification of the breach and may include substantial fines, public or private reprimands, and activity-related measures. An ordinary charger manufacturer is not automatically an AML-obliged entity solely by reason of its industry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers or officers may face personal administrative or criminal consequences where their own conduct or statutory responsibility meets the applicable legal standard; sanctions are not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deducting or withholding tax from dividends, interest, royalties, payroll, or other payments and failing to file or remit it when due.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer may owe the withheld tax, surcharges, interest, and applicable penalties. Criminal liability may arise only where the facts meet the elements and thresholds of a criminal offence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur subsidiary or other personal liability only under statutory conditions, including the applicable culpability and enforcement requirements.
